technical_issues.issue: States RAAN initial value indicates launch facility location - RAAN determined by launch time/ascending node crossing, not site latitude; also Argument of Latitude u=0 listed as static rather than time-varying.
Selects Vega E (first flight 2024 unproven in 2020 report) and claims two launch windows per day because latitude 5.05deg N < target inclination, conflates inclination constraint with RAAN window.
Altitude 600 km drag-sail passive deorbit within 25-year guideline plausible but no decay calculation shown; swath vs reef width discussion qualitative.

overall: Solid preliminary SSO reef-monitoring design with single satellite, STK analysis and EOL drag sail. Well justified for Australia, meets all major task elements with good evidence.

feedback.summary: You produced a solid preliminary SSO reef-monitoring design with clear Australian benefit. Your single-satellite rationale, STK-supported orbit and ground-station analysis, and defined users/operators are strong. To strengthen the report, correct orbital-mechanics details, justify launch vehicle choice with proven flight history, add quantitative EOL decay, and improve referencing and figure numbering.
next_steps: In Mission Design - Orbit, correct that RAAN is set by launch time not facility latitude, and show argument of latitude u as time-varying; remove static u=0 from elements table.

In Mission Design - Launch, justify Vega vehicle selection against 2020 flight heritage (Vega C vs unproven Vega E) and fix the two-windows-per-day explanation to address RAAN alignment, not just latitude < inclination.

In Mission Duration & EOL and Ground Control, add a hand calculation or STK lifetime run for the drag sail at 600 km and quantify swath vs reef coverage and contact budget to support your 580s mean access claim.

criteria.C1: You did well framing the primary mission as fluid lensing reef monitoring for bleaching, and clearly justifying one satellite and users like CSIRO, BOM and government. Your literature links support the rationale. For full Accomplished, add more specific user data needs and cite peer-reviewed sources consistently.
criteria.C2: You provided detailed launch from Guiana on Vega E, SSO parameters a=6971km, 600 km, i=97.79deg, e=0, STK 3D views and ground tracks, and 580s mean access via Mount Pleasant. To reach top of Accomplished, provide decay calculations for drag-sail deorbit, correct RAAN and launch-window reasoning, and quantify swath coverage.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion synthesises launch, polar SSO with constant sun angle, ground station, and EOL, linking back to bleaching monitoring and 2025 launch risk. To strengthen to higher Accomplished, explicitly evaluate trade-offs and key performance against mission requirements with numbers from your design.
criteria.C4: You used a clear structure with Executive Summary, TOC and headed sections; writing is readable. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, number all figures/tables consistently for cross-reference, format references in-text with a consistent style instead of raw URLs, and proofread for grammar.
